issues.legal_issue: A provision imposing personal tax liability on members of a divided family does not apply retrospectively to assessments completed under the prior tax law when the family had undergone only a partial partition.
material_facts: A family’s movable property was partially partitioned before the relevant assessment years, while the family otherwise continued to exist.
The tax assessments for the relevant years were completed under the prior tax law, which did not make family members personally liable for tax following a partial partition.
The later recovery orders sought to allocate the family’s tax debt among its members and make them personally liable.
issues.conclusion: The new provision imposing joint and several personal liability could not be applied to assessments completed under the prior tax law; the tax could not be recovered personally from the family members under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 25A of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1922, personal liability following assessment of a Hindu undivided family arose on a recorded total partition, not a partial partition. Section 171(6), read with Section 171(7), of the Income Tax Act, 1961 introduced personal liability in cases of total or partial partition. Applying the presumption against retrospectivity, a provision that creates a new liability does not apply to earlier assessments unless the statute expressly or by necessary implication requires it. The Court referred to Additional Income-Tax Officer v. Thimmayya in explaining Section 25A and to the general interpretive rule stated in Halsbury’s Laws of England, Vol. 36, 3rd ed.

predicates.tax_recovery_after_family_assessment: The proceeding seeks to recover tax assessed against a family from its members after the family has divided.
predicates.assessment_completed_under_prior_law: The family’s tax assessment was completed under a tax law that applied before the law imposing the disputed personal liability.
predicates.family_partially_partitioned: The family divided some, but not all, of its property among its members.

issues.definition: When tax is being recovered from family members after an assessment under the prior law and the family only partially partitioned its property, the members are not personally liable for the assessed tax.

issues.legal_issue: A transitional provision allowing the successor tax law’s procedures to be used to reassess escaped income does not apply that law’s new substantive personal liability to tax years governed by the prior law.
material_facts: Assessments for earlier tax years were reopened after the successor tax law came into force because income had escaped assessment.
The reassessments were made using the successor law’s procedure for reopening assessments.
The recovery orders relied on a new provision that imposed personal liability on family members, a liability not imposed by the law governing the earlier tax years.
issues.conclusion: The transitional provision made the successor law’s assessment machinery applicable to the reopened assessments, but did not import its new substantive personal-liability provision; the prior law governed that liability.
issues.legal_principle: Section 297(2)(d)(ii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, read with Sections 147 and 148, permits the successor law’s provisions to apply when escaped income from an earlier year is reassessed. The words “all the provisions of this Act shall apply accordingly” refer to the machinery for assessment and do not incorporate substantive provisions creating new rights or liabilities. The substantive law governing liability remains the law applicable to the relevant tax year; Section 171(6) is substantive because it creates personal liability.

predicates.reassessment_of_earlier_year_escaped_inc: The proceeding reassesses income alleged to have escaped assessment for a tax year that occurred before the successor law applied.
predicates.reassessment_under_successor_law_procedu: The reassessment proceeds under the successor law’s procedures for reopening assessments.
predicates.asserted_member_liability_is_substantive: The recovery sought would impose on family members a personal tax liability that did not exist under the law governing the relevant tax year.

issues.definition: When escaped income from an earlier year is reassessed using successor-law procedures and the asserted member liability is a new substantive liability, the successor law does not impose that liability.
